jobs.description: About Tritium Fuel Cycle (TFC)  GFG is designing a first-of-a-kind (FOAK) fusion power plant (FPP) to deliver 1 GW of electrical power in the 2040s. The “GIGA” plant will be based on a stellarator magnetic confinement fusion device, operating continuously on a deuterium-tritium (D-T) fuel cycle.  Prior to this, the smaller “Gauss Industrial Demonstrator (GID-170)” will be deployed in the mid-2030s.   While deuterium can be extracted from seawater, tritium is a tightly controlled radioactive isotope with an extremely limited global supply. Therefore, both GID-170 and GIGA must utilise closed tritium fuel cycle infrastructure, to ensure that unburnt tritium is fully recycled back to the stellarator and not released to the environment. Meanwhile, the tritium consumed by the fusion reaction must be replenished using tritium breeding blankets (TBB).
